title: Enforce one bounded control frame per WebSocket message and eliminate attach bootstrap deadlock
description:
## Finding

The WebSocket client accepts a large binary message containing many encoded control frames, copies and repeatedly shifts the remaining buffer while decoding them, then can deadlock before returning `AttachStream`.

## Evidence

* `crates/thegn-core/src/control_wire.rs:9` specifies one encoded frame per WebSocket binary message.
* `crates/thegn-svc/src/control/client.rs:947-961` nevertheless drains every embedded frame from one message.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/control_wire.rs:539-563` copies the message, copies each payload, and shifts the full remaining `Vec` for every frame, yielding quadratic work for many tiny frames.
* WebSocket connections use tungstenite defaults at `client.rs:734,749,841,856`, allowing an outer message far larger than the 1 MiB inner payload cap.
* `start_attach` forwards all frames from the first message into a fresh 256-slot channel before returning the receiver. Hello plus 256 additional frames blocks forever on the 257th send because no receiver exists yet.

## Required design

1. Configure WebSocket frame/message limits to the control-wire cap plus fixed framing overhead.
2. Reject any binary message that does not contain exactly one complete control frame.
3. Decode with a cursor/advance strategy that performs at most linear work and one bounded compaction.
4. Validate Hello, return the stream, and start the pump before any post-bootstrap forwarding; malformed bootstrap data must fail rather than queue.
5. Apply the same policy to event subscriptions and pane attach.

## Acceptance criteria

* A Hello-plus-extra-frame message is rejected and cannot deadlock connection establishment.
* Oversized WebSocket frames/messages fail before large allocation.
* Decoder complexity remains linear for adversarial inputs.
* Tests cover 257 tiny frames, concatenated frames, declared payload over cap, fragmented transport frames, and clean one-message/one-frame traffic.

## Dependency mapping

* Independent wire/transport root.
* Directly blocks strict greeting and downstream stream-state work.
* Related to THE-273 (handshake/body deadlines) and THE-184 (bounded stream consumers). Neither is a prerequisite.
